subtopic_title: Construction of parallel and perpendicular lines.

record_links.rationale: This record defines the task of constructing a perpendicular line through a given point.

record.evidence_quote: Lines that are perpendicular **intersect** each other at right angles (at $90^{\circ}$). When we are asked to construct a **perpendicular line**, we will be given one of the lines, as well as a point. We then have to construct a line through the given point so that the new line is perpendicular to the given line.

record_links.rationale: This worked example gives the straightedge-and-compass procedure for constructing a perpendicular from a point on a line.

heading_path.h3: Worked example 14.1: Constructing a perpendicular line from a point on the line

record.evidence_quote: You are given line $AB$ with a point $P$ on the line. Construct line $PQ$ so that $PQ$ is perpendicular to $AB$.
record.prompt_text:
You are given line $AB$ with a point $P$ on the line.

Construct line $PQ$ so that $PQ$ is perpendicular to $AB$.
record.answer_text:
Step 1: Mark equal distances to both sides of point $P$ on line $AB$.

Put the compass on point $P$. Draw an arc to the left of point $P$. Then, while keeping the compass open by exactly the same amount, draw an arc to the right of point $P$. These arcs should intersect line $AB$.

Step 2: Draw an arc from the left.

Put the compass point on the arc at the left. Draw an arc so that it is above point $P$.

Step 3: Draw an arc from the right.

Keep the compass exactly the same width open as for Step 2. Put the compass point on the arc at the right. Draw an arc so that it intersects the arc from Step 2.

Step 4: Draw the perpendicular line.

Point $Q$ is where the two arcs from Step 2 and Step 3 are intersecting each other. Use a ruler and draw a line from point $P$ and through point $Q$.

Step 5: Check your construction.

Use a protractor to measure $Q\hat{P}A$ and $Q\hat{P}B$. If each of them is equal to $90^{\circ}$, you have made an accurate construction.

record_links.rationale: This construction hint supports accurate perpendicular-line construction and checking.

record.evidence_quote: When copying the lines in order to do constructions, the lines only need to be more or less the same length as given in the questions, and in more or less the same direction. It is a good idea to rotate your workbook if you have to do a construction involving a line that is not horizontal on the page in front of you. N

heading_path.h3: Worked example 14.2: Constructing a perpendicular line from a point away from the line

record.evidence_quote: You are given line $AB$ with a point $P$ away from the line. Construct line $PQ$ so that $PQ$ is perpendicular to $AB$.
record.prompt_text:
You are given line $AB$ with a point $P$ away from the line.

Construct line $PQ$ so that $PQ$ is perpendicular to $AB$.
record.answer_text:
Step 1: Mark equal distances from point $P$ on line $AB$.

Put the point of the compass on point $P$. Draw an arc to the left of point $P$ on the line. While keeping the compass exactly the same width open, draw an arc on the line to the right of point $P$. These arcs should intersect line $AB$.

Step 2: Work from the left and draw an arc below line $AB$.

Put the compass point on the left arc of Step 1. Draw an arc so that it is underneath point $P$.

Step 3: Work from the right and draw a second arc below line $AB$.

Keep the compass the same width open as for Step 2. Put the compass point on the arc to the right arc of Step 1. Draw an arc so that it crosses the arc from Step 2.

Step 4: Draw the perpendicular line.

Point $Q$ is where the two arcs from Step 2 and Step 3 cross each other. Use a ruler and draw a line from point $P$ and through point $Q$.

Step 5: Check your construction.

Use a protractor and measure the angles where line $AB$ and line $PQ$ intersect. If each angle is equal to $90^{\circ}$, you have made an accurate construction.
